candidate_relations.reason: Biopsy showed diabetic nodular glomerulosclerosis without an acute glomerulonephritis pattern.
The biopsy explicitly found no acute interstitial nephritis, so AIN conflicts with the documented histology.
Moderate pericardial effusion with early right-atrial collapse is a concurrent cardiac finding, not oxalate nephropathy.
Early diastolic right-atrial collapse suggests tamponade physiology accompanying uremia, not the renal histologic diagnosis.
Anion-gap 25 with beta-hydroxybutyrate 7.8 mmol/L documents DKA as a concurrent metabolic crisis, not the oxalate nephropathy.
Acute tubular injury/necrosis is present on biopsy but omits the defining multifocal oxalate crystal deposits.
Creatinine 6.2 mg/dL and eGFR 7 describe severe AKI without the oxalate mechanism.
Klebsiella oxytoca urinary infection is a concurrent infectious finding, not oxalate nephropathy.
